businessVision: ProjectOS delivers ordinary technical work on real projects end to end: Claude implements, the ChatGPT gatekeeper reviews through the trusted broker without the owner's relay, and ProjectOS carries each approved phase through checks, review, commit, push and closure; where the owner has delegated the closure commit to ProjectOS, a phase closes with no owner act at all, and the owner holds every protected action.
definitionOfComplete: Nine phases are complete: the temporary pieces created for the live proofs are retired and spending is disabled once the key is revoked (PROJECTOS-COMPLETION1A); and before it: one `projectos continue` carries a phase from work to closed, a phase that changes its own required validator is judged by that new copy as well as the base copy, and a third agency phase proves both with no owner act; and before them: phase write grants come from a structured list of paths in the approved plan, with the judging validators run from the last approved commit; phase closure works for any governed project; the ChatGPT gatekeeper answers without the owner's relay through the trusted broker (owner decision of 2026-10-25); ProjectOS has carried one ordinary phase end to end on a new governed project, the website of an SEO and social-media posting agency, with evidence; a project whose owner grants the closure-decision-commit scope has its delegate's closure decision committed by ProjectOS itself, with a model-invented decision time refused; and a second agency phase has closed end to end with no owner act. Host-attested unattended review, the signed installer, Forge and the Control Center redesign are deferred and are reopened only by an owner decision.

phases.title: Stage 1 exit proof: cross-provider review and a refusing cap, live
phases.description: One governed Develop phase closes from one continue where the reviewer (Codex CLI, OpenAI) is a different provider from the implementer (Claude Code), and a deliberately low cap is shown to refuse a provider call. Evidence only. Runs AFTER PROJECTOS-KERNEL-FOLLOWUP1A, which builds the Codex reviewer adapter, and AFTER PROJECTOS-KERNEL-CODEX-LIVE1A, which fixes what the live probe found, AFTER PROJECTOS-KERNEL-PLAN-HISTORY1A, which lets a pre-D11 project plan again, AFTER PROJECTOS-KERNEL-CODEX-UNC1A, which stops the UNC tripwire refusing an innocent review, and AFTER PROJECTOS-KERNEL-REVIEW-READONLY1A, which keeps the reviewer to reading and carries its findings to the gatekeeper (the planning engine keeps this phase before the appended follow-up). The second provider is not xAI/Grok (owner, 2026-10-29); the gatekeeper uses the current OpenAI key (owner: "Keep the current key"; rotation after project completion).

phases.title: Codex reviewer: fixes from the live sandbox probe
phases.description: The EXIT-PROOF1A precondition probe (2026-10-29, live Codex CLI 0.165.0 on this host) showed: with --ignore-user-config and no Windows sandbox mode Codex can run no command at all (every read "rejected: blocked by policy"), so the reviewer could never review; with windows.sandbox set (elevated or unelevated) reads work and writes inside and outside the checkout are blocked ("Access to the path ... is denied"); Codex reports every command wrapped in an absolute powershell.exe -Command, which the out-of-checkout heuristic reads as a path outside the repository, refusing every review; both sandbox modes can still read the owner profile (the residual the owner accepted as tripwire-only: "Accept tripwires (Recommended)"). This phase makes the adapter set the Windows sandbox mode itself (fixed, not configurable) and analyse the command inside a known shell wrapper.
phases.scope: Edit the Codex adapter, its tests and its validator rules only.
exclusions: No relaxation of any owner gate, closure eligibility predicate or ownerOnlyActions.
The Codex adapter stays reviewer-only, read-only sandbox, no credential argument; the sandbox mode is fixed by the adapter, never taken from project configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: On Windows the adapter always passes a fixed Windows sandbox mode; a configured argument cannot change or remove it; tested.

A command reported inside a known shell wrapper (absolute powershell.exe/pwsh.exe -Command, cmd.exe /c, bash -lc) is judged by its inner command; an unknown wrapper or an inner command reaching outside the checkout is still a denial; tested with the exact forms the probe recorded.
Every new rule has a validator pin and a named mutation.

phases.title: D11 at plan approval: closed phases are history
phases.description: Setting up the Stage 1 exit proof, the agency plan v1.4 was refused PLAN_INCOMPLETE because D11 R5 ("every phase needs an independent review") was applied to the agency's three phases that CLOSED before D11 existed. A closed phase is history: no review can now be added to it, and refusing every later plan for it leaves a pre-D11 project unable to plan at all. R5 is now skipped for a phase only when it is already in the ACTIVE approved plan AND its COMMITTED phase record says closed; a new or open phase still needs an independent review. Owner: "Fix ProjectOS properly (Recommended)", 2026-10-30, approving the change to the protected planApproval.ts.
phases.scope: Edit planApproval.ts and the role-review validator; add tests.
exclusions: No relaxation for any phase that is not both in the active approved plan and closed by a committed phase record.
No change to any owner gate, closure eligibility predicate or ownerOnlyActions.
acceptanceCriteria: A plan whose only self-review-only phases are closed (committed record) and already in the active plan is approved; the same phase not closed, closed only in the working tree, or absent from the active plan is refused; tested.
The role-review validator pins the exemption to exactly those two conditions with named mutations.

phases.title: Codex reviewer: the UNC tripwire reads a quoted escape as a path
phases.description: The exit proof's first run (2026-10-30 09:30, agency SEO-AGENCY-SITE-CHECK3A) had its Codex review refused as "attempted tools it was denied". A traced re-run of the same adapter path against the same candidate showed the only denial was a false positive: the reviewer piped a Node probe script into node, and the script's JavaScript string "\\nExpires: ..." (a quote followed by an escaped newline) matched the UNC tripwire as the network path \\nExpires. Nothing left the checkout. A denial ends the run on the owner, so this false positive alone defeats the zero-owner-act exit proof. This phase makes the UNC tripwire require a host followed by a separator (\\host\share, //host/share, \\?\UNC\..., \\.\pipe\...), which every path into a share has, and which a quoted escape does not. The exit proof runs after it.
phases.scope: Edit the Codex adapter, its tests and its validator rules only.
exclusions: No relaxation of any owner gate, closure eligibility predicate or ownerOnlyActions.
No other tripwire is narrowed: home, .codex, parent escape, POSIX home, absolute paths, fetch/decode and the credential-shaped reply checks stay as they are.
acceptanceCriteria: The exact command the exit proof's reviewer ran is not a denial; \\host\share, //host/share, \\?\UNC\host\share and \\.\pipe\name paths still are; tested.
The UNC rule has a validator pin and a named mutation that is killed.

phases.title: Independent reviewer: review by reading, say why a review was refused, carry a rejection's findings
phases.description: The exit proof's second run (2026-10-30 10:56) had its Codex review refused again as "attempted tools it was denied", with no record of which tripwire fired. Five traced reviews of the same candidate showed why: Codex writes and runs Node scripts that execute the candidate's own validator, and those scripts trip the text tripwires on innocent content (a JavaScript ".." string read as a parent escape; a failed script whose output carried git's own sandbox warning "unable to access '.../.config/git/ignore': Permission denied"). With one added sentence telling the reviewer to review by reading only (git diff/show/log and file reads; no scripts; run no repository code, the loop already ran it), three of three traced reviews ran no script, tripped nothing, and still found the candidate's real defect. Separately, a reviewer REJECT whose findings are all MEDIUM or LOW reaches the gatekeeper as "returned REJECT" with no finding text, so the gatekeeper cannot name a correction. This phase: (1) adds the read-only reviewing sentence to the review instruction; (2) names the reviewer's denial reasons in the refusal; (3) carries a rejection's findings (bounded, inert) into the stop detail when none is CRITICAL or HIGH; (4) ignores git's own config-access warning line when deciding that a failed Codex command was stopped by the sandbox. The exit proof runs after it.
phases.scope: Edit the review instruction, the independent review refusal and objection texts, the Codex adapter, their tests and validator rules only.
exclusions: No relaxation of any owner gate, closure eligibility predicate or ownerOnlyActions.
No tripwire is narrowed except the one git warning line, matched exactly; a reviewer rejection still credits nothing and stays non-approvable.
acceptanceCriteria: The review instruction tells the reviewer to review by reading only and to run no script or repository code; tested and pinned.
A review refused for denied tools names the denial reasons, bounded and inert; tested.
A REJECT with only MEDIUM or LOW findings puts those findings (bounded, inert) in the stop detail; a REJECT still credits no review; tested.
A failed Codex command whose only sandbox-shaped output is git's config-access warning is not a denial; any other sandbox wording still is; tested and pinned with a named mutation.
